MIDI_CV_MTS_ESP.notes: This is VCV's own MIDI-CV with an MTS-ESP client added. The retuning is applied in semitones on top of the MIDI note number (MIDI_CV_MTS_ESP.cpp:99-102), so the pitch output follows the master's tuning while a note is held unless the note-on-only menu item is set. A note the master filters out is skipped before the parser sees it (lines 79-83), so no gate is produced for it either.

CV_MIDI_MTS_ESP.notes: This is VCV's own CV-MIDI with an MTS-ESP client added. With a master connected the pitch voltage is turned into a frequency and the master is asked which note that frequency belongs to (CV_MIDI_MTS_ESP.cpp:93-96), so the note number follows the master's mapping rather than twelve-tone tuning; with no master it falls back to twelve semitones to the volt around note 60.

A 10V pulse 1ms long on a channel whenever that channel's output pitch changes

Note — a master has to be loaded elsewhere: in a VCV Host module in this patch, or in any application on the same computer, since MTS-ESP passes tunings between processes

Note — the output is worked out again at most every 5ms and holds its last value between those
Note — notes the master has marked as filtered out are skipped in quant mode, so the output never lands on them

Quantizer_MTS_ESP.notes: Quant mode searches the master's 128 tuned frequencies for the two either side of the input and picks one by the rounding switch; retune mode rounds to a twelve-tone note first and then looks that note's frequency up, so the two modes can give different answers for the same input (Quantizer_MTS_ESP.cpp:105-140). With no master the module is a wire: line 154 onwards copies the input to the output.

Interval.notes: The bend and transpose CV jacks are read wrongly for polyphonic cables: Interval.cpp:96-99 loops over the channels but reads getVoltage(0) inside the loop, so every channel takes the first channel's voltage, and channels above the cable's count are set to 1 rather than 0. The numerator and cents displays occupy the same place on the panel and only one is shown at a time, so a click reaches whichever the Interval Mode switch has chosen.
